text: Thank you for that detailed history. Given your past history of colon cancer, it is crucial to determine if this swelling is related to metastasis or a new primary issue. text: The swelling feels firm and non-tender. It is somewhat mobile over deeper structures but seems adherent to the skin. I have not experienced any significant weight loss or night sweats.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the history of colon cancer and the nature of the swelling, I need to rule out metastasis or an abscess. The patient appears generally healthy with no systemic symptoms like fever or weight loss, and the swelling is described as firm, non-tender, and adherent to the skin on the nape of the neck. Given the location and chronicity in a diabetic patient, this presentation is highly suggestive of a pilomatrixoma or an epidermoid cyst, though metastasis must still be considered given his cancer history.
